findings.text: Host exit preserves the full host general register file into the host context, invokes trap handling, then restores the same file before returning. A companion entry resumes only the restore phase from a caller supplied context pointer.

The host exception table routes only synchronous exceptions from the host execution states toward host handling, while all hypervisor exceptions and all host interrupt, fast interrupt and error classes take invalid paths.

Host hypercalls inspect the requested function number and either enter full exit handling or transfer to stub handling through an identity mapped target while preserving leading argument registers. Protected operation always selects full exit.

Hypervisor panic establishes masked exception return state targeting the host panic routine, optionally disables second stage translation with invalidation, gathers syndrome and address information plus vcpu association, then re enters the host with or without register restoration depending on context availability.

Monitor forwarding reloads host general registers from the supplied context, issues a single monitor call, then writes results back into the same context while retaining the context pointer in a register preserved across the call.

Early initialization exposes a minimal vector where only synchronous exceptions from one host mode reach setup logic. That logic diverts low function numbers to stub handling, rejects mismatched init identifiers, otherwise invokes low level setup with caller parameters and reports success.

Per CPU startup provides distinct power on and resume entries converging on shared initialization. The shared path verifies privileged execution level, configures exception state, enables translation and vectors, then returns to a host address held across setup.

Stub handling supports a soft restart that reprograms exception return state and reshuffles arguments, a vector reset that disables translation and installs stub vectors, and a generic error return for other requests.

Protected initialization can replace translation base and stack by disabling translation, invalidating hypervisor entries, installing a new base and stack, then restoring prior control before returning to a caller supplied address.

Protected vcpu loading, unloading and current loaded query are exposed for host coordination. Load resolves a handle and index to a hypervisor vcpu, put releases it, and query returns the calling CPU resident instance.
Virtual machine resolution from an opaque handle is available to other hypervisor code when the table lock is held.
A single hypervisor spin lock serializes table lookup, lifecycle checks, slot publication and consumption, residency flags and reference counting across load and unload.

Handle translation subtracts a fixed base and rejects out of range indices and reserved entries. Load additionally rejects dying guests, indexes beyond created vcpus, unpublished slots and double loading elsewhere.

At most one vcpu is resident per physical CPU and a given hypervisor vcpu is resident on at most one CPU. Successful load pins the owning guest and records residency in two places; unload clears both and drops the pin.

Guest and host vector state are each moved under their respective maximum lengths, with hypervisor length control set to the side being moved and the host maximum restored afterwards. Scalar state follows the same save then restore pairing.

Floating point synchronization is inactive unless the guest owns the registers. When active it orders prior trap changes, saves guest state in vector or scalar form, preserves optional matrix extension state when present, restores host state and marks host ownership.

Interrupt state moved toward the hypervisor clamps the list count to hardware capacity, copies only that many entries, fixes enable controls to a constant permitting signalling with default routing, and preserves control state. The reverse move copies control, virtual control and active entries back.

Bulk state copying transfers general registers, saved status for several exception classes, floating point registers and almost all system registers, but deliberately leaves timer offsets, values and controls for direct host management.

Flushing toward the hypervisor clears the running marker, copies debug controls, interrupt flags and error syndrome state, and merges only host owned control bits including wait trapping and pending virtual error state while preserving the remainder. Protected guests copy the whole context; others copy on dirty indication with different host masks.

Synchronization back to the host always returns fault and interrupt state plus virtual interrupt state. Protected guests return the whole context, while other guests return only program location and processor state because detailed state synchronizes on demand.

Debug state follows an ownership marker. Guest owned moves guest breakpoint and watch state in both directions, host owned moves external debug state and its control copy, and otherwise only the marker moves.

Loading a protected vcpu propagates only wait trapping controls from the host request, while loading other vcpus refreshes fine grained trap controls from host state. Unloading a clean non protected vcpu writes hypervisor state back first.

Per CPU initialization parameters aggregate stack address, memory attributes, hypervisor control, thread identifier, second stage base and control, page table base and translation control used during early setup.

A vcpu context holds general registers with program location and state, separate saved status for fast interrupt, abort, undefined and interrupt, floating point and vector state, an indexed system register file, plus interrupt, debug, trap control and lifecycle fields shared between host and hypervisor images.

CPU initialization progresses from level verification through exception state setup, translation enablement and vector installation to host return. Cores not starting at the privileged level never advance and remain in low power wait. When extended configuration is active, exception setup is replayed while preserving parameters across the sequence.

Hypervisor vcpu residency cycles among unloaded, loaded active and released. Load fails if the CPU already holds one or the target is held elsewhere; put returns to unloaded and balances the guest pin.

Floating point ownership toggles between host owned and guest owned. Flush unconditionally claims host ownership without moving data, while synchronization moves state toward the host only from guest owned and then claims host ownership.

Panic entry tolerates a missing host context by skipping restoration before exception return, and the non restoring return path must not disturb any registers. The panic restore path deliberately preserves argument registers.

Translation changes require invalidation and completion barriers around control updates, and authentication key swaps require ordering before use. Early setup also discards bootloader entries for both hypervisor and host regimes, and panic teardown pairs control clearing with invalidation.

Concurrent loads could observe a partially published vcpu or resurrect a dying or reserved guest without serialized checks and acquire ordering; the implementation holds the table lock across validation, residency marking and reference adjustment.

Guest identity, stub dispatch and init invocation use fixed encodings: handles offset into a bounded table with a reserved sentinel, low call numbers divert to stub handling, and init success or unsupported status is reported through standard call result codes after masking hint bits.

Host context, initialization block and exception return state use stable layouts: ordered general register slots, named init fields for translation and CPU state, and masked exception status selecting host handler mode with syndrome and fault addresses delivered in fixed argument registers.
